transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (CISO - Cedarbridge), Maya Singh (Security PM), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (auto generated, may be incomplete): Quick posture review, request for SOC2/ISO artifacts, Trust Center access, KMS details and audit log formats.

00:00 Jared Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, Jared from Redwood here, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:10 Daniel Ortiz: Good, thanks. Appreciate you fitting this in - we're on a pretty tight compliance timeline for our audit next quarter.
00:16 Priya Nair: Totally, yeah we know timelines can be tight. We'll try to cover the big checks: where the reports live, how to access the Trust Center, and then dive into things like RBAC/SSO and KMS.
00:30 Maya Singh: Great. Specifically we need to confirm that we can map Redwood controls to our ISMS controls and that evidence formats are compatible. Also audit logs retention is a big one.
00:42 Jared Kim: Understood. Quick intro: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and an ISO 27001 attestation, both updated annually. We host artifacts in our Trust Center and can grant read-only access to security teams.
00:58 Liam O'Connor: When you say Trust Center, is that a portal we sign into? SSO? Or do you just ship PDFs?
01:06 Priya Nair: It's a portal. We can invite enterprise security teams with SAML SSO and role-based permissions. For some customers we also share password-protected PDF links. We'll walk through the access model in a second.
01:20 Daniel Ortiz: Ok, can you confirm whether the SOC2 has a carve-out for subservice organizations, and what scope you used? For example, are infra providers like CloudX listed?
01:31 Priya Nair: Yes, the SOC 2 includes standard subservice disclosures. Cloud provider names are present in the report; we also include a controls mapping appendix that shows which controls we map to common frameworks.
01:44 Maya Singh: And ISO? Do you have the scope statement available? We need to confirm our shared boundary for processing PHI-adjacent data.
01:51 Jared Kim: We have an ISO 27001 certificate and a scope statement; we'll share the attestation and the scope doc. For PHI specifically, Redwood's hosted service is not a BAA by default, but we do have Private deployment options for regulated workloads.
02:06 Daniel Ortiz: Right, so we'll probably need to look at Private deployment or Dedicated if we can't sign a BAA for hosted.
02:12 Priya Nair: Yep. For Dedicated we can provide reserved pools and tighter network controls; Private gives you a customer-controlled VPC and on-prem options with our private control plane.
02:23 Liam O'Connor: For KMS, what options do you support? Customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS or HSM?
02:30 Priya Nair: We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private. For hosted customers we have an option to use Redwood-managed keys but we can integrate with customer KMS in Dedicated/Private via key wrapping or envelope encryption patterns. HSM integrations are possible for Private deployments.
02:50 Daniel Ortiz: How is key rotation handled? And do you log key usage for audit?
02:55 Priya Nair: Rotation policies can live in the customer's KMS; Redwood records key usage events in our audit logs when keys are used for encrypt/decrypt operations. Those logs are available via the Trust Center and can also be streamed to customer SIEMs for Dedicated/Private.
03:14 Maya Singh: Is the audit log schema documented? We have field mapping requirements for our ingestion pipeline.
03:19 Priya Nair: Yes, we have a sample log format in the controls mapping docs; we'll attach a sample CSV/JSON. The logs include timestamps, request IDs, actor, resource, action, result, and key ID for KMS ops.
03:34 Daniel Ortiz: What about retention? We need 7 years for certain logs.
03:38 Jared Kim: By default we retain 365 days in the Trust Center, but for Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention and export to your S3 or SIEM. We can discuss retention SLAs in the contract.
03:51 Liam O'Connor: SAML and SCIM? We need provisioning and group sync for RBAC.
03:56 Priya Nair: We support SAML for SSO and SCIM for provisioning in enterprise tiers. RBAC is role-based with tenant-level roles; we can map to your identity groups. Also we have audit trails for admin changes.
04:12 Daniel Ortiz: Do you support context-aware access or conditional MFA enforcement?
04:16 Priya Nair: Conditional access is typically enforced at the IdP layer. We can support enforcement via SAML attributes and require MFA from the IdP. Redwood logs when admin sessions are created.
04:28 Maya Singh: Controls mapping - will you provide a spreadsheet mapping Redwood controls to our ISMS control IDs? We need to drop that into our evidence binder.
04:35 Jared Kim: Yes, SE will produce a controls mapping spreadsheet that aligns SOC 2 sections and ISO controls to common control IDs, plus sample evidence pointers (screenshots, timestamps, log extracts).
04:48 Daniel Ortiz: One point - our auditors want to see who exactly accessed production data and when. Does Redwood surface user-level access to model calls or just service accounts?
04:59 Priya Nair: We log request-level metadata including API key ID, requestor identity when using SSO tokens or user-bound keys, timestamps, and resource IDs. For hosted customers, if you're on a shared tenancy, identity mapping requires SSO link; for Dedicated/Private it's straightforward to get user-level traceability.
05:20 Liam O'Connor: Is there a standard retention export? Like a daily push to our S3?
05:26 Priya Nair: Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can push logs to your S3 or stream to Kinesis/Logstash. For hosted we can provide on-demand exports or limited streaming via enterprise connectors.
05:40 Maya Singh: Regarding data residency: our legal team requires EU-only processing for certain datasets. How do you guarantee regionally isolated processing?
05:50 Jared Kim: We have region controls and can pin workloads to regions. For Hosted, you can select EU regions and we ensure processing in-region. For strict guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can manage the network boundary.
06:04 Daniel Ortiz: Any SOC2 exceptions or major findings in the last cycle?
06:08 Priya Nair: Nothing materially adverse. There were minor findings around patching timelines which we've closed; we'll share the remediation summary.
06:18 Maya Singh: Can we get evidence of periodic penetration tests?
06:22 Jared Kim: Yes, annual pen tests and vulnerability scans; we have summaries and some redacted reports we can share under NDA if needed.
06:31 Daniel Ortiz: On reports, can we get them via our GRC platform? We use SecureBinder - can you publish evidence there?
06:38 Priya Nair: We can export artifacts; for integrations with GRC tools we frequently provide S3 exports or direct uploads depending on the tool. We'll take a note to check SecureBinder compatibility.
06:52 Liam O'Connor: A bit more detail on KMS key IDs in logs - will the key IDs be the full ARN?
06:56 Priya Nair: Yes, logs contain key IDs and ARNs for easy correlation. We can also redact or hash KIDs on request in exports.
07:10 Daniel Ortiz: For the Trust Center invite, what permission levels exist? We just need read-only for auditors and a full admin for our platform leads.
07:17 Jared Kim: We support granular roles: viewer, auditor, admin. Viewer is read-only for reports and logs, auditor can download evidence, admin can manage invites and settings.
07:28 Maya Singh: How long does it take to get Trust Center invites set up?
07:31 Priya Nair: Typically same-day for enterprise accounts; we'll request an SAML IdP metadata or send an invite link.
07:38 Daniel Ortiz: On the legal side - BAA? Our legal says we need a BAA for PHI.
07:43 Jared Kim: Redwood doesn't automatically sign BAAs for hosted at the lower tiers; we have a process for enterprise contracts that can include a BAA for Dedicated or Private deployments. We'll coordinate with legal on the path.
07:58 Maya Singh: If we go Dedicated, are we able to require customer-managed encryption keys?
08:03 Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated and Private support CMKs. We'll detail key management patterns in the deep dive.
08:12 Daniel Ortiz: Any SLAs tied to audit log availability? We need guarantees of log delivery within a certain SLA window.
08:18 Priya Nair: We can define delivery SLAs in Dedicated contracts	6 e.g., daily export within 24 hours, streaming within minutes depending on connector. We'll capture your exact SLA needs in follow-up.
08:34 Liam O'Connor: A small note: we may need fuller request traces (payload hashes) rather than full payloads for PII protections. Is that supported?
08:42 Priya Nair: Yes, we can include payload hashes in logs instead of full request bodies, and we have data masking options.
08:52 Daniel Ortiz: Good. For proof-of-concept scoping, what would you recommend we run to validate audit logs and KMS flows?
08:58 Jared Kim: A short POC: spin up a Dedicated instance, enable CMK, send test requests from your app, and validate log exports to your SIEM. SE-led 2-week run usually suffices.
09:14 Maya Singh: That sounds reasonable. What's the expected cost band for a short Dedicated POC?
09:19 Jared Kim: We'll send pricing but for a small Dedicated pool for a 2-week POC it's usually a fixed evaluation fee; I'll include ranges in the follow-up.
09:30 Daniel Ortiz: Are there any known limitations on export formats for audit logs? We need JSON lines with ISO timestamps.
09:36 Priya Nair: JSON lines with ISO8601 timestamps is our standard; CSV exports also possible. We'll attach sample format.
09:47 Maya Singh: On mapping controls, can you include which artifact types correspond to each control (e.g., console screenshot, log extract, config file)?
09:55 Priya Nair: We'll annotate the spreadsheet with artifact types and provide examples.
10:05 Daniel Ortiz: Ok, recap would be helpful.
10:09 Jared Kim: Sure. Action items: we'll send SOC2 & ISO artifacts, invite you to the Trust Center read-only, SE will prepare controls mapping and sample logs, and we'll schedule the KMS/audit-log technical deep dive.
10:24 Maya Singh: Timeline: we'd like Trust Center access this week and the deep dive next week if possible.
10:30 Jared Kim: We'll aim to get the Trust Center invite out today and schedule the deep dive	6 Priya will follow up with a Doodle.
10:40 Daniel Ortiz: Perfect. Anything else?
10:43 Priya Nair: Just to note competitors - we discussed BigCloudAI earlier; if you have specific comparisons we'll include notes in the follow-up.
10:52 Daniel Ortiz: Thanks all.
10:55 Jared Kim: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
